headline: Primo Brands grows sales, margins slip, raises outlook
summary_short: Q1 2026 net sales rose 0.8% y/y to $1,626.1M, but gross margin fell 370bp to 28.6% and net income from continuing operations was $27.3M ($0.07 diluted EPS) as transportation, integration, and D&A costs weighed on margins.
summary_long: Q1 2026 net sales rose 0.8% y/y to $1,626.1M on premium-brand and Direct Delivery growth, partly offset by exited OCS business. Gross margin fell to 28.6% from 32.3% on higher transportation, integration, and D&A costs. Net income from continuing operations was $27.3M ($0.07 diluted EPS); Adjusted EBITDA fell 10.4% to $306.0M (margin -240bp to 18.8%). Operating cash flow rose to $103.8M from $38.8M, but $118.1M of capex and intangible additions left free cash flow at $(14.3)M. The company raised full-year organic sales growth guidance to 1%-3% (from 0%-1%) and widened Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1,465M-$1,515M (from $1,485M-$1,515M). Cash fell to $288.2M; long-term debt was $5,082.4M. Quarterly dividends were $44.2M; buybacks totaled $29.0M.

drivers.explanation: Premium-brand growth in Retail channels and continued Direct Delivery improvement, partly offset by the exited US Office Coffee Services business not recurring this year.
Gross margin fell to 28.6% from 32.3% on higher transportation-related costs, non-recurring integration costs, and increased depreciation and amortization.
Gross-margin contraction outpaced a roughly flat SG&A ratio (SG&A $336.7M vs $327.8M, steady as % of net sales).
Tracks the decline in operating profitability; the release states no further below-the-line explanation for the change.
Follows lower net income, partly offset by a lower diluted share count (365.8M vs 381.6M y/y) from continued buybacks.
Company's own Adjusted EBITDA fell 10.4% on the same gross-margin pressures (transportation, integration costs, D&A) cited for gross profit; margin compressed 240bp to 18.8%.
Rose to $103.8M from $38.8M; the release does not itemize the working-capital or timing drivers behind the increase.
Cash fell from $449.7M to $288.2M, reflecting $44.2M of dividends, $29.0M of share repurchases, and $118.1M of capex/intangible spending in the quarter not fully offset by operating cash flow.

Held roughly flat at $5,082.4M; no refinancing activity is disclosed in this release (a separate credit-agreement amendment was executed the same day as the quarter-end, per a different 8-K, but falls outside this earnings release).

Management called it a strong start to 2026 with top-line results ahead of expectations; raised full-year organic net sales growth guidance to 1%-3% and widened (not simply lowered) full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance amid inflationary cost pressure.
